attrs.content: UAV Companion: an open-source map of suitable-flight (适飞) zones for most mainland Chinese provinces and no-fly zones for Singapore, from official and third-party reference data. You can check a spot, save places and plan trips. It is reference information, not flight advice: check the official platform for your location before every flight.

elements.text: Map app for Open and Navigate
Automatic (Amap in China, Google Maps elsewhere)
Amap only covers China, so Google Maps is used anywhere else. The Open and Navigate icons share the place's coordinates with the map app, only when you tap one. Saved in this browser only.
Hours above this limit are shown in red in the weather card. Saved in this browser only.
Show the dashboard when the app starts
Off keeps it tucked behind the ^ tab at the bottom of the map.
A trip groups markers. A waypoint's distance to accommodation or a home point only looks within its own trip. Your Home marker belongs to no trip.
No trips yet. Create one, then choose it for new markers or tag existing ones.
(same as the start for one day)
Ask any AI assistant to turn your itinerary into markers: copy the prompt, add your itinerary after it, then paste the answer here. You see a preview first, and nothing is added until you confirm.
Tap to choose a type and place it on the map

elements.text: Press and hold a place for 1 second, then drag it to another day or stop. Alt + ↑ / ↓ moves it from the keyboard.
No markers yet. Choose a type above, then tap Place on map.

Most helpful online features are on by default; each one sends only what its card says, and every switch here turns it off. Automatic location sharing and automatic attendance stay off until you agree. As a guest, your markers, trips, notes and settings are kept in this browser; map tiles and any feature you leave on still contact the services named below. Signing in adds a cloud copy and social features.
Shows the next 5 hours in each marker window. Sent when you place a marker and when the page loads (at most every 30 minutes), to Open-Meteo.com. On by default.
Rounded to about 1 km. The forecast is the same, because its grid is 10 to 25 km. Recommended.
About 10 m. Shares the exact spot for no gain in forecast accuracy.
This applies to the "Show weather here" button as well.

Shown in marker windows and when you check a point, using Open-Meteo.com. On by default. Always sends the exact marker or point location (about 10 m), whatever the weather setting: at 1 km the ground can differ by hundreds of metres in the mountains.
Look up places by name when importing

For itineraries from an AI: a place that came without coordinates is searched by its name or address. Those names are sent to Photon (Komoot), or Nominatim (OpenStreetMap) if Photon fails, only when you press Add on an import. On by default. Looked-up places are marked unverified.
Centre the map on me when the app opens

The browser asks for your location when the app opens. If you allow it for this site, the map opens on where you are; if you do not, it opens where you left off. Your position is only used on this device and is never sent anywhere.

Off until you agree: the app asks once, the first time a friend or a shared-trip member is online. Once on, and while you are signed in, your location is shared with them in future sessions without switching anything on, only while this page is open, and the browser still asks for location permission. Sharing stops when no eligible friend or member is online, or when you press Stop. Nothing is sent otherwise. The Stop button on the map ends it, and a switch you turn off by hand stays off until you turn it on again. Off: sharing starts only when you switch it on.
Friends who are online see you on their map, marked as a friend. Off: only trip parties are included.

While this page is open and a session you joined is under way, your position is sent to UAV Companion every 30 to 60 seconds so the server can check that you are at the meeting point. The server keeps only times and a count, never your position. Nothing runs in the background, and it works only when you are signed in.
Look for public sessions near the map centre

On by default once you are signed in; as a guest nothing is requested unless you switch this on. The dashboard asks UAV Companion's server for public sessions within 10 km of the map centre, rounded to about 1 km. It uses the map centre, never your position.

On by default. Uses your position to enable a Check in button on a marker when you are within 300 m of it, and the browser asks for location permission first. Your position is read only while the panel shows markers and is never sent anywhere. A check-in saves your coordinates and the time with the marker, in this browser.

Every marker shows its straight-line distance to your nearest Home. A waypoint also shows its nearest Home point and Accommodation, only from its own trip and only those whose dates overlap its own (one with no dates counts for every date). If a waypoint is farther than the max range from every such Home point and Accommodation, it is shown in red; your Home does not count toward the range. Units also set the map's scale bar. Elevation and height limits stay in metres.

A short log of problems (failed requests, errors) is kept in this browser only: at most 500 entries, 200 KB and 7 days. It holds no positions, marker names, notes, tokens or account details, and nothing is sent anywhere. Download it if someone is helping you with a problem.

the basemap you pick is loaded from OpenStreetMap, OpenStreetMap France (the Humanitarian and CyclOSM styles), OpenTopoMap or CARTO (standard OSM in dark mode), which see which area you view. CARTO receives your IP address and page origin; .
online search sends your query to Photon or Nominatim, only when you search. Name lookup on import does the same with the names in the import (on by default; switch it off above).

on by default; your position is read by the browser only while check-in is on and the panel shows markers. It is saved with the marker in this browser, included in an export, and left out of share links.
Open-Meteo.com. Weather uses rounded coordinates (about 1 km) unless you choose Precise; elevation uses the exact marker or point location. Both are on by default and can be turned off above.

these go to UAV Companion's own server (Supabase): the rounded map centre for nearby public sessions (on by default when signed in; for a guest only if switched on), your position for live sharing (signed in, once you agree), and position samples for automatic attendance (signed in, once you and the server have agreed).
